description: The same questions over up to 1000 states, several requests at a time: triage postings, transactions, emails or passages without reading them all yourself. Replies with a summary per question (choice: counts; noul: mean and how many are >= 0.7 and <= 0.3; score: mean, min, max) and each row's compact answers (a noul's probability, a choice's pick and confidence, a score and its confidence). For a large batch pass list 'none' or 'failed' with save true: every row's full answers go to a JSONL file in the outbox and the reply names it with its sha256 and size. A row that fails is reported and the rest go on. Rows already in a file go as items_file, not typed into items: that keeps them out of your context and exactly as written. thresholds turn each answer into act, review or abstain; where lists only the rows that meet conditions, top only the k highest by a question, and counts tallies the answers (and verdicts) of the rows where keeps: over a large batch they keep the reply to the rows that matter. A client that asks for progress hears the rows done; cancelling stops the rows not yet asked.

counts.description: Also tally each question's answers (a noul's yes/no/between, a choice's picks, a score's nearest levels) and verdicts over the rows where keeps.

items.description: The rows, typed into the call. Give items or items_file.

id.description: Names the row in the answer. Default: its index, allowed only up to 20 rows.

state.description: What is judged: text, or JSON with named fields (a record, a thread, a posting with its metadata) the questions can point at, e.g. `posting.location`.

items_file.description: The rows as a UTF-8 file instead of items: JSONL, one {"id", "state"} object per line, or one JSON array of them; at most 1000, every row with an id above 20. The reply names its sha256 and size. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-_odad58g), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

path.description: A path: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-_odad58g); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

list.description: Which rows the reply lists; the summary always covers every row.

model.description: A model from health. Default: the server's, jev-latest.

probabilities.description: Also list each row's full distribution per choice and score.

oneOf.description: Yes/no: answered with the probability that the answer is yes.

criteria.description: What a yes and a no mean, when the question alone leaves room.

instructions.description: The judgment, stated in full (question ids never reach the model). An object may hold the question in one field and data it refers to in others, pointed at in backticks.

oneOf.description: One of a defined set: the pick, a probability per option, and a confidence.

criteria.description: Option -> what it means (null when the name says it all). Include a "none" option when nothing may fit.

instructions.description: The judgment, stated in full (question ids never reach the model). An object may hold the question in one field and data it refers to in others, pointed at in backticks.

oneOf.description: A degree on your ordered levels: a probability-weighted value from 0 (can land between levels), per-level probabilities, a confidence.

criteria.description: Ordered levels, lowest first, each a concrete situation that stands on its own.

instructions.description: The judgment, stated in full (question ids never reach the model). An object may hold the question in one field and data it refers to in others, pointed at in backticks.

questions.description: Your question id -> question. Every independent judgment about the same state goes in one call: they run together and cannot see each other.

save.description: Also write every row's full answers to the outbox as JSONL.

act_above.description: Act on the answer when its certainty is above this.

review_above.description: Otherwise a person reviews it when its certainty is above this; below, abstain. At most act_above.

thresholds.description: Question id -> thresholds: each row's answer to that question gets a verdict, act, review or abstain, taken on its certainty (a noul's |p - 0.5| x 2, a choice's or a score's confidence, rounded down to three places). The reply echoes them and the summary counts the verdicts.

top.description: Only the k rows (of those where keeps) with the highest value for one question, highest first.

by.description: A noul or score question id: rows are ranked by its p or its score.

anyOf.description: A noul: true is a yes (p >= 0.7), false a no (p <= 0.3), as the summary counts them.
A choice: its pick is this label.
A choice: its pick is one of these labels.

is.description: As the shorthands: true/false for a noul, labels for a choice.

max.description: The row's value at most this.

min.description: The row's value at least this: a noul's p, a score, a choice's confidence.

where.description: Question id -> condition; the reply lists only the answered rows meeting every one, and says how many matched. E.g. {"urgent": true, "team": ["billing"], "mood": {"min": 1.5}}. Checked against the questions before any request.
